title: P0-3r cli-resume-analysis: Add suspended_at_step.is_some() guard to analyze_resume
description: Bug P0-3r (revision of black-hat-rejected vb-nkfta). Black-hat review round 1 found that cmd_resume IS already wired at run_ops.rs:150 (the original 'no-op' framing was fabricated). The real bug is in crates/vb_cli/src/commands_journal.rs analyze_resume (lines 386+). When the journal contains NO WaitScheduledEvent or AskScheduledEvent, suspended_at_step is left as None, but can_resume: true is still returned. This means a fresh run with no suspension events reports 'can resume' even though there is nothing to resume from. The fix: add a guard `if suspended_at_step.is_none()` BEFORE the terminal check; if no suspension indicator was found, return can_resume: false with reason 'run has no suspension events; nothing to resume'. Master §33.3 lifecycle: resume is for suspended runs, not runs that have just started. Kani harness: prove analyze_resume on a journal with zero WaitScheduled/AskScheduled events returns can_resume == false. proptest: 100 random journal sequences assert can_resume is true iff (suspended_at_step.is_some() AND !is_terminal).

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL return can_resume=false from analyze_resume when no WaitScheduledEvent or AskScheduledEvent exists in the journal
THE SYSTEM SHALL preserve existing analyze_resume behavior when the journal contains a WaitScheduledEvent or AskScheduledEvent

event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL return ResumeAnalysis { suspended_at_step: Some(5), can_resume: true, .. } (preserved behavior)

unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT return can_resume: true regardless of suspension events
unwanted.because: Terminal runs cannot be resumed; the existing terminal check is correct and must be preserved
